messages.subject: MLF
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I have been googling a lot and could not find much literature about the MLF function in lavaan (maximum likelihood estimation with standard errors based on the first-order derivatives, and a conventional test statistic).

When should this function be used? How is it compared to ML and ML with robust standard errors? Regarding non-normal data, which one is better, MLF or MLR/MLM?

Of course if you can point to some articles discussing MLF, I would be very grateful.

Best,
Edo

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: MLF
parts:
> When should this function be used? How is it compared to ML and ML with
> robust standard errors?

Point estimates are the same. Only different approach to compute
standard errors. See any test on maximum likelihood estimation to learn
about the three different information matrices: observed, expected, and
first-order.

Regarding non-normal data, which one is better,
> MLF or MLR/MLM?
